documents.title: Standards for Licensed Assisted Living Facilities (22VAC40-73), revised effective September 23, 2026
documents.issuer: State Board of Social Services / VDSS Division of Licensing Programs
documents.version: Amended by the State Board August 17, 2026; effective September 23, 2026 (the PDF shows 09/26)
documents.how_used: I found no separate policy-review checklist for ALFs. The regulation is the controlling list, because the application tells the applicant to submit everything 'required by the regulations to be developed'. Items below are the sections that require written policies, procedures, plans, programs, agreements or statements. Item IDs follow the regulation's own section and subsection numbering.

documents.title: Initial Application for a License to Operate an Assisted Living Facility (ALF)
documents.how_used: Part 3, 'Required Attachments for Initial Application', is the checklist the reviewer uses. Items 15, 16, 17, 20 and 21 are the policy and program content. The remaining Part 3 items are excluded as application paperwork: references, entity documents, budget, credit reference, administrator license, building, fire and sanitation inspections, floor plan, management company name, staff information sheet, pet certificates and fee.

documents.title: Instructions: Initial Application for Licensure (Part II Program Addendum noted)
documents.how_used: Used only for submission mechanics: which pages to submit, the budget and credit reference, and the 60-day lead time. It does not list policy content.

required_items.text: A copy of all rules, requirements or policies and procedures of the Assisted Living Facility required by the regulations to be developed.
Written documentation of the program's 'chain of command' or organizational chart, including all individuals responsible for operational and management decisions.
A copy of the Disclosure Statement.
Sample current menu for a two-week period.
Sample current monthly activity schedule.

Program of care that meets residents' physical, mental, emotional, psychosocial and spiritual needs; promotes highest level of functioning; provides protection, guidance and supervision; promotes security, self-worth and independence; promotes involvement with appropriate programs and community resources.

Licensee shall exercise general supervision over the facility and establish policies and procedures concerning its operation in conformance with applicable law, this chapter and the welfare of residents.

Written disclosure statement on the department's form, in plain language, provided before admission and signing of agreement and on request, kept current. It covers: facility and licensee name; ownership structure; accommodations, services and care; fees; admission criteria and restrictions; transfer criteria; discharge criteria; activities (categories, frequency, number); staff number, positions and qualifications per shift; onsite emergency power source (items powered, staff trained, signed acknowledgment); note that more information is in the resident agreement; DSS website address.

If electronic signatures are used: specific policies and procedures for their use, plus controls (name and title identified, document unalterable, limited access, signed user statements, strong evidence of validity). Back-up and security system for all electronic documents.

Incident reporting: report major incidents to the regional licensing office within 24 hours (content per B); written report within seven days signed by the administrator (content per C(1)-(10)); amendments (D); keep copies two years (E); resident-record documentation (F).

If the facility assists with resident funds: signed and dated request and delegation, funds kept separate, resident choice of account type, reasonable fee (not for auxiliary grant recipients), written accounting at least quarterly, funds available on request.

If licensee, administrator or staff acts as attorney-in-fact or trustee: documented request, accountability, written accounting at least quarterly, funds available on request, return of funds with full accounting on termination.

Develop in writing and implement an infection control program addressing surveillance, prevention and control of disease and infection, consistent with CDC guidelines and OSHA bloodborne pathogens regulations. A licensed health care professional trained in infection prevention participates in development. Administrator ensures at least an annual documented review. A trained staff person is point of contact.
Program applies to all staff and volunteers and encompasses all services and the entire premises.
Procedures for infection prevention by staff and volunteers: standard precautions; personal protective equipment; hand hygiene.

Procedures related to job duties: screening prospective or returning residents for acute infectious disease; safe injection practices and blood/body fluid exposure; blood glucose monitoring (no shared fingerstick devices); linens, supplies and equipment handling; room sanitation; equipment sanitation; medical waste; pest control program.
Accessible handwashing equipment and PPE; product-specific instructions for cleaning and disinfecting agents; initial training (22VAC40-73-120 C 4) and annual retraining of staff and volunteers.

Staff health program: vaccination information per CDC ACIP; assurance that employees with communicable diseases are identified and kept from work activities that could transmit them; bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan; documentation of screening and immunizations (including hepatitis B access); OSHA reporting compliance.
Immediate report of a disease outbreak to the local health director or VDH Commissioner and to the regional licensing office; follow VDH recommendations to prevent or control transmission.

General staff qualifications: considerate and respectful of residents' rights, dignity and sensitivities; able to speak, read, understand and write English as needed for the job; background check compliance (22VAC40-90).

Orientation and training within the first seven working days. Orientation (B(1)-(7)): purpose of the facility, organizational structure, services, daily routines, policies and procedures, duties of the position, regulatory compliance as it relates to duties. Training (C(1)-(10)): emergency and disaster plans; resident emergencies; first aid kit; handwashing, standard precautions and infection control; confidentiality; resident rights and responsibilities; detecting and reporting abuse, neglect or exploitation (§ 63.2-1606); incident reporting (22VAC40-73-70); adjustment problems on moving in; for direct care staff, residents' needs, preferences and routines.

Mandated reporters report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation under § 63.2-1606; facility notifies the resident's contact person or legal representative of a report without identifying confidential information.

Administrator responsibilities include developing and implementing all policies, procedures and services required by the chapter, ensuring residents' rights, maintaining the buildings and grounds, recruiting, hiring, training and supervising staff, and ensuring the individualized service plan for each resident (except residents with independent living status).

If a shared administrator or a combined ALF/nursing home administrator is used: written management plan for each facility describing how the administrator will oversee care, supervision and day-to-day operation; designated manager where applicable.

Designated direct care staff person in charge when the administrator, assistant or manager is not on duty: duties determined by the administrator; staff trained on duties and given written documentation of them before being placed in charge.
Administrator develops and implements a written plan for supervision of direct care staff who have not yet met the qualification requirements.

Direct care staff annual training: 14 hours (residential only) or 18 hours (both levels); starts within 60 days; at least two hours on infection control; at least four hours on mental impairments where applicable; documentation kept by individual.

Private duty personnel: obtain written information on services before they start; reflect services on the ISP; apply tuberculosis requirements; orientation on facility policies; documentation of care; monitoring. If not from a licensed home care organization: qualification documentation, criminal history review, and a written facility policy (B(3)(c)) on private duty personnel and criminal history.
Written agreement with any resident who performs staff duties (duties, hours, compensation; voluntary; not a condition of admission).

Volunteers: appropriate qualifications, confidentiality, criminal record clearance or supervision, documentation (C(1)-(5)), duties differentiated from staff, a staff volunteer coordinator, orientation with signed statement, supervision when residents are present.
Staff records (A-C(1)-(11)) and health requirements (D(1)-(4) tuberculosis screening, E vaccination record).
First aid and CPR certification of staff, with posted listing of certified staff and certified staff present on off-premises activities.

Training when aggressive or restrained residents are in care: self-protection and de-escalation; restraint application, monitoring and skin care; training criteria and written description; at least annual refresher training.

Staffing adequate in knowledge, skills and number. B: maintain a written plan specifying the number and type of direct care staff needed, tied to actual resident acuity and care needs. Also: staff to implement the fire and emergency evacuation plan; awake direct care staff; background checks before direct contact.
Written work schedule with names and job classifications for each shift and who is in charge; keep two years. Develop and implement a procedure for posting the name of the on-site person in charge.
Procedures for communication among administrators, assistants, managers and staff in charge; written communication method keeping direct care staff on all shifts informed; keep record two years.

Admission and retention criteria: no admission or retention where care cannot be provided; determination of ability to meet needs before admission (B(1)-(4): UAI, physical exam report, documented interview, mental health screening); use and occupancy classification (C); written assurance of appropriate license (D); age 18+ and consent (E-F); rights not waived (G); prohibited conditions (H(1)-(12)); stage III ulcer, intermittent IV, and gastric tube provisions (I-L); hospice written agreement with policies and procedures for communication and coordination, roles, ISP reflection and signatures (M(1)-(4)).
Physical examination and report within 30 days before admission (content per A(1)-(13)); subsequent tuberculosis evaluations (B).
Written fall risk rating for residents meeting assisted living care criteria; review annually, on change of condition and after a fall; documented analysis and interventions after a fall.
Mental health screening (when required, by a qualified mental health professional) and notification of service needs; psychosocial and behavioral history obtained and used for admission and the ISP.
Sex offender information: register with State Police, ascertain registered sex offender status before admission, inform residents with written acknowledgment, and offer assistance and printed copies.

Emergency placement requirements (documented and approved, maximum seven days). Respite care exceptions (ISP before respite, reevaluation each return, new physical exam after six months, dates in record, medication review not applicable).
Resident personal and social information obtained prior to or at admission and kept current.

Resident agreement or acknowledgment signed at or before admission. It covers financial arrangements (A(1)(a)-(g)); rules on resident conduct and restrictions; actions that could result in discharge; and acknowledgments (A(4)(a)-(n)). The acknowledgments cover conduct rules, notice to move, pet policy, weapons policy, § 63.2-1808 and the facility's policies for implementing it, release of information, resident council, bed hold policy, visiting policy, smoking rules, medication and dietary supplement policy, liability insurance and written license assurance. Copies are retained and updated as policies change.

Monthly itemized statement of charges and payments. Resident orientation on admission (emergency response procedures, mealtimes, call system) with signed acknowledgment, plus a written description of staff types and services and hours.

Procedures to ensure a resident detained by a temporary detention order is accepted back if not involuntarily committed (written recommendations from a QMHP, documentation of whether they can be implemented, ISP update, staff communication).

If the facility allows temporary movement with a bed hold, a written bed hold policy: conditions, time frames, terms of payment, and when the bed will no longer be held (consistent with auxiliary grant policy for AG recipients).

Discharge: discharge planning begins immediately, resident moved within 30 days with exceptions documented (A); notices (B); written policy on number of days notice a resident must give, not exceeding 30 days (C); assistance (D); emergency discharge (E-F); public pay notifications (G); discharge statement (H(1)(a)-(d)); information to the receiving facility (I); final accounting within 60 days (J).
Uniform assessment instrument completed face to face before admission, at least annually and on significant change, by qualified assessors per 22VAC30-110.

Individualized service plans: preliminary plan of care (A); comprehensive ISP within 30 days (B, C(1)-(6)); hospice coordination (D); signatures (E); review at least every 12 months (F); filing and access (G); deviations (H).

Personal care services and general supervision: resident-centered care; supervision including fall and wandering prevention; observation and documentation of changes; 24-hour notification of falls or wandering; language access; assistance with ADLs, IADLs, ambulation, hygiene and grooming, and functions and tasks (H(1)-(5)); clean clothing; incontinence care; personal care items.

Health care services: ensure health care needs are met (A); skilled nursing treatments (B); prevent clinically avoidable complications (C); D: develop and implement a written policy to make staff aware of allergies, allergic reactions and life-threatening conditions of residents and actions staff may need to take; medical attention for serious accident or illness with 24-hour notification (F); refusal of medical attention (G).
If unlicensed staff provide gastric tube care: informed consent, delegating RN, staff approval and competency, supervision schedule, written protocols (E(8)), and a written back-up plan (E(9)).
Restorative, habilitative and rehabilitative services.

Health care oversight by a retained licensed health care professional (frequency per resident level: A(1)-(3)); scope of oversight (B(1)-(8)); additional oversight for restrained residents (C(1)-(7)); written certification (D); documented response (E).

Reasonable access for community services boards and behavioral health authorities. Mental health services coordination: secure services; B: written procedures to ensure communication and coordination between the facility and the mental health service provider; documented efforts; contracts provided to the licensing office within 10 days.

Activity program: supports skills, variety, weekly mix of activity types (A); participation (B); planning (C); at least 11 hours per week (residential only) or 14 hours per week (both levels), at least one hour each day (D-E); staffing and leader understanding (F-G); supplies (H); I: written schedule developed at least monthly, posted, kept two years; outdoor access (J); unscheduled interaction (K).

Freedom of movement. Visitation: daily visits permitted, hours not restricted; C: facility may establish a visiting policy or guidelines; E: protocol for clergy visits during a declared public health emergency.

Resident rights: grievance process (B); D: operator or administrator shall establish written policies and procedures for implementing § 63.2-1808; E: make those policies available and accessible to residents, relatives, agencies and the public; F: posting of rights and required telephone numbers; G: annual review of rights with residents and staff; H: responsible individual for residents unable to exercise rights.

Resident records: A: establish written policy and procedures for documentation and recordkeeping; identification, confidentiality, locked storage, access, retention (two years after leaving) and a current picture.
Release of information: release form available to residents and legal representatives; limited circumstances for release without permission; information sent to the hospital or EMS.

Food service and nutrition: VDH compliance reports; meals in the dining area and room-service policy and agreement (B); assistance and meal time (C-D); E: policy to monitor each resident for nutrition-related changes and compliance with needs; F: weight monitoring and interventions; independent living status residents (G).
At least three well-balanced meals daily and snacks always available; meal interval limits (15 hours evening-to-breakfast; at least four hours between other meals).

Menus: resident food preferences considered; weekly menus dated and posted; substitutions recorded; menu record kept two years; minimum daily menu (C(1)-(4)); prescribed diets; current diet manual (E); drinking water (F).
Oversight of special diets at least every six months by a dietitian or nutritionist, on site, with written certification. Respect residents' religious dietary practices.
Facility shall have, keep current and implement a written plan for medication management addressing procedures for administering medication.
Methods to ensure understanding of medication management responsibilities; standard operating procedures, including the standard dosing schedule and facility-specific restrictions.

Methods to prevent use of outdated, damaged or contaminated medications; ensure prescriptions and OTC drugs and supplements are filled and refilled timely; verify orders are transcribed to MARs within 24 hours.
Methods for monitoring administration and effective MAR use; MARs maintained in the resident record; accurate controlled substance counts whenever assigned medication staff change.
Methods to ensure medication staff meet the qualification requirements of 22VAC40-73-670; are adequately supervised, including periodic direct observation; plan for proper disposal of medication.

Methods to prevent administration of medications or supplements to which residents have known allergies; identification of the person responsible for communicating medication issues to the prescriber; methods to ensure staff are trained on the plan; procedures for internal monitoring of conformance to the plan.
The written medication management plan requires approval by the department; later changes reviewed at regular inspection; keep a pharmacy reference book or drug guide no more than two years old.

Medication practices the plan must be consistent with: physician or prescriber orders (650); storage (660); qualifications and supervision of medication staff (670); administration, MAR content, errors, PRN, stat-drug boxes (680 A-N); medication review (690 A-G).

When oxygen therapy is provided: valid order; no-smoking signs; portable source outside rooms; emergency numbers; staff training; and a checklist in the disaster preparedness plan for residents on oxygen (generator capacity, vendor agreements, chart copies of vendor agreements, transport of equipment).

Restraints: chemical, prone and supine restraints prohibited; physical restraint only as medical/orthopedic support or in an emergency; physician order, monitoring, consent, notification and documentation requirements.

DNR orders: valid written order included in the ISP; system to make staff aware; F: if DNR orders will not be honored, the facility shall have a policy specifying this, and the resident is notified before admission and signs an acknowledgment.

Advance directives: obtain contact information, location and content of directives; document efforts if unable; keep information available to EMTs; refer residents who request help establishing directives.

Each facility shall develop and implement a written policy regarding procedures when a resident's clothing or other personal possessions are reported missing: determine the reason, take reasonable action to recover the item and prevent future losses, report results in writing to the resident, keep documentation at least two years.

Transportation assistance; mail not censored and delivered promptly; telephone access and privacy; smoking only in designated areas approved by the fire official, ashtrays, no smoking in bed, smoke-free areas.
Resident councils: permit and encourage formation, assist with meetings and written responses, annual reminder if no council exists.

Written policy regarding pets living on the premises: types of pets permitted and conditions; immunizations and veterinary certification; regular examinations; restricted from food preparation areas; documentation; humane treatment; no compromise of resident rights or needs; suitable temperament.
If pets may visit: written policy regarding visiting pets; pets in good health; no compromise of residents' rights or needs; well-treated and safe temperament.

Each facility shall develop and implement a written policy regarding weapons on the premises that ensures the safety and well-being of residents and staff; if firearms are permitted, procedures ensure ammunition and firearms are stored separately in locked locations.

Use and occupancy classification and building official documentation; plans submitted to the department for review before construction or remodeling; hazardous materials and cleaning supplies stored locked.

The facility shall develop and implement a plan to protect residents from heat-related and cold-related illnesses in the event of loss of air-conditioning or heat due to emergencies or equipment failure.
Signaling and call systems; hourly rounds with a written log in buildings of 19 or fewer residents lacking an origin-identifying signal; ISP and rounds plan for residents unable to use the device.

Emergency preparedness and response plan, in writing, addressing documentation of initial and annual contact with the local emergency coordinator (local disaster risks, communitywide plans, assistance available).
Analysis of the facility's potential hazards, including severe weather, biohazard events, fire, loss of utilities, flooding, work place violence or terrorism, severe injuries, or other emergencies.

Written emergency management policies and procedures for: administrative direction and management of response; coordination of logistics; communications; life safety of residents, staff, volunteers and visitors; property protection; continued services to residents; community resource accessibility; recovery and restoration.

Written emergency response procedures for assessing the situation; protecting residents, staff, volunteers, visitors, equipment, medications and vital records; and restoring services. They address alerting personnel; warning and notification of residents; emergency access to secure areas and locked doors; evacuation and sheltering in place with resident accounting; shutting off utilities; operating emergency equipment; communicating with staff and responders; relocation to emergency shelters or alternative sites.

Supporting documents needed in an emergency: emergency call lists, building and site maps to shut off utilities, memoranda of understanding with relocation sites, list of major resources such as suppliers of emergency equipment.

Facilities with an on-site generator describe its capacity (lighting, ventilation, temperature control, oxygen, refrigeration) in the plan. Facilities without one enter agreements with two separate vendors capable of providing an emergency generator.

Staff and volunteers prepared to implement the plan; E(1)-(6): orientation and semi-annual documented review for all staff, residents and volunteers; F: annual review and signed plan revisions; G: appropriate action during a disaster; H(1)-(2): after stabilization, notify families and legal representatives and report to the regional licensing office by the next day.
Written fire and emergency evacuation plan approved by the appropriate fire official; evacuation drawing posted on each floor; emergency telephone numbers posted; staff and volunteers informed.
Fire and emergency evacuation drills per the Statewide Fire Prevention Code; unannounced; evaluated with corrective action; record kept two years (E(1)-(9)).

Written plan for resident emergencies: handling medical emergencies, including who calls the rescue squad or physician and who provides first aid and CPR; handling mental health emergencies; making medical information and history available to the rescue squad and hospital; missing-resident procedures (staff and law enforcement involvement, areas searched, expectations on locating, documentation); notifying family, legal representative, contact person and social agency; notifying the regional licensing office per 22VAC40-73-70.

Review of the plan with all staff at least every six months with signed documentation; staff practice exercise every six months; plan readily available to staff, residents' families and legal representatives.

Emergency equipment tied to the plan: first aid kit(s); permanent connection for temporary emergency power at 6+ residents; generator or connection testing and records; emergency lighting; two forms of emergency communication; 96-hour food and drinking water supply.

If residents have serious cognitive impairments (mixed population): two awake direct care staff, cognitive impairment training (administrator 12 hours, direct care staff six hours, other staff two hours), security monitoring of doors, window protection, outdoor access, indoor walking area, environmental precautions.

If operating a safe, secure environment (special care unit): independent written assessment before admission, written approval by priority order, written appropriateness determination with six-month and annual review, activities program (21 hours per week, at least two hours daily, designated coordinator), staffing ratios, staff training (administrator 12 hours, direct care staff 10 hours), doors and windows, outdoor access, indoor walking area, environmental precautions and enhancements.

The operator or administrator shall establish written policies and procedures to ensure that, at the minimum, each resident: (1) is informed of rights and rules, with written acknowledgment; (2) is informed of services and charges, with a signed agreement; (3) manages personal finances and receives quarterly accounting when delegated; (4) has confidential treatment of affairs and records; (5) is transferred or discharged only with a statement of reasons and reasonable notice; (6) participates in care planning and may refuse treatment; (7) is not required to perform services except by voluntary agreement; (8) selects health care services; (9) may refuse human subject research; (10) is free from abuse, neglect, exploitation and forced isolation; (11) is treated with courtesy, respect and dignity; (12) is encouraged to exercise rights and may voice grievances without reprisal; (13) may retain personal clothing and possessions; (14) is encouraged to function at his highest potential; (15) is free of restraint except as permitted; (16) is free of unnecessary prescription drugs; (17) has privacy (a)-(f); (18) may participate in social, religious and community groups; (19) is informed about registered sex offenders; (20) is informed of liability coverage on request.
required_items.cite: Va. Code § 63.2-1808 A(1)-(20), reproduced as the Attachment to 22VAC40-73 and cross-referenced by 22VAC40-73-550 D

required_items.text: Responsible individual for residents unable to exercise rights; rights printed and posted with required phone numbers; policies and procedures for implementing the section available and accessible to residents, relatives, agencies and the public; staff training on each right.

Part II Administration and Administrative Services
Part V Admission, Retention and Discharge of Residents

Part VII Resident Accommodations and Related Provisions

notes: VDSS does not publish a stand-alone ALF policy checklist. The reviewer's hook is Part 3, item 16 of Initial Application 032-08-0100-03-eng (07/26): submit a copy of all rules, requirements or policies and procedures required by the regulations to be developed, plus the organizational chart (#17), disclosure statement (#15), two-week sample menu (#20) and monthly activity schedule (#21). The application is submitted to the Division of Licensing, 5600 Cox Road, Glen Allen, VA 23060, at least 60 days before the planned opening date. If the application is incomplete, the applicant is notified within 15 days and has 30 days to complete it. Organize the manual in the regulation's order (Parts II-IX, then Part X if applicable, then the § 63.2-1808 policies), using the 22VAC40-73 section numbers as headings so the inspector can map each policy to a standard. The medication management plan (22VAC40-73-640) is the only item the regulation says requires department approval (B). The licensing inspection tool says the infection control program and medication management plan are to be provided if changed, and all required policies must be readily available at inspection. DSS also posts an Infection Prevention and Control Policies and Procedures Manual Template, a Disclosure Statement form, a Liability Insurance Statement form, a Medication Administration Record and an Individualized Service Plan form on https://www.dss.virginia.gov/licensed-care/assisted-living-facilities-alf/. I did not open those forms. Part VII physical-plant, Part VIII building and Part IX supply items (such as 980, 750-780 and 860-925) are omitted unless they require a written policy or plan. Items marked 'if applicable' apply only when the facility uses that practice (electronic signatures, resident funds, shared administrator, hospice, gastric tubes, pets, room service, bed holds, safe secure unit). The Instructions (dated 2/14) are older than the 07/26 application and do not list policy content. The regulation text fetched is the version effective 9/23/2026. The task brief says further amendments take effect 11/4/2026; I could not confirm that from the fetched PDF, so check for changes before submitting. I also did not review the 2026 legislative implementation memo, which covers the AED requirement and resident electronic monitoring.
